title: A thin dipole at its resonance
shows: A 0.5 m dipole of 0.1 mm wire (length 5 000 radii) fed at its centre and swept through half a wavelength: a thin dipole's reactance vanishes when it is about 0.48 wavelengths long, where its input resistance is about 70 Ω (73 + j42.5 Ω at exactly half a wavelength is the induced-EMF estimate for a sinusoidal current, which a real wire does not carry).
source: Thin-dipole resonance: C. A. Balanis, Antenna Theory, 4th ed. (2016), §4.6 and §8.5; R. W. P. King, The Theory of Linear Antennas (1956).
